findings.title: Legacy hosts are skipped and then deleted
findings.body: `embeddable_hosts` is the result of a `SELECT`, and PostgreSQL reports zero affected rows via `cmd_tuples` for a SELECT. This condition therefore skips copying the legacy host list, but line 31 still deletes the old settings. Upgrading a site with configured hosts loses its allowlist, so previously working embeds are rejected.

findings.title: An unset legacy embed category aborts the migration
findings.body: `embed_category` is optional and defaults to an empty value; if it is unset or does not match a category, this join returns no rows. Indexing `[0]['id']` then raises before the migration can fall back to the uncategorized category, preventing the upgrade. Handle an empty result before accessing the row.

findings.title: Host lookup does not normalize both sides consistently
findings.body: The saved host is only stripped of its scheme and path, while `URI(host).host` omits any port and preserves hostname casing; the query lowercases only the stored column. Consequently, a host accepted with a port (the validation explicitly allows ports) will never match, and an uppercase hostname in a request will fail to match a lowercase stored host. Normalize both values consistently so valid hosts are not rejected.

findings.title: Duplicate host rows can assign embeds to the wrong category
findings.body: There is no uniqueness validation or database index on `host`, so the admin UI can create multiple rows for the same hostname with different categories. `first` selects only one row, meaning the chosen category depends on which duplicate is returned and later edits to another duplicate may have no effect; newly imported topics can be assigned to the wrong category. Enforce one mapping per host.
